input.reasoning:
Estimate derived from backlog story points (total = 5+8+8+13+8+5+13+21+8+8+5+5+8+13+8+5+8+13+8+8+5+8+5+8 = 202 points). Using a standard conversion of ~6 hours of blended engineering effort per point (a common mid-complexity SaaS assumption, adjusted up for known-complex items like migration, payments, RBAC), total engineering effort ≈ 1,250 hours before role-splitting overhead. This was then split across roles based on task nature (backend-heavy items: auth, RBAC, payments, migration, audit, email, search, currency, rate limiting, observability; frontend-heavy: dashboard, design system, invoice UI, ticket UI, admin UI, analytics UI, responsive/accessibility; QA effort scaled at ~18% of total dev hours reflecting 0.6 FTE capacity; DevOps effort scaled at ~8% reflecting 0.4 FTE capacity for CI/CD, observability, decommission, migration infra).

Capacity check: 1.5 FTE Backend = 1.5*40=60 hrs/week; 1.0 FTE Frontend = 40 hrs/week; 0.6 FTE QA = 24 hrs/week; 0.4 FTE DevOps = 16 hrs/week. Total team capacity ~140 hrs/week. Allocated total hours (~1,480 across roles) implies ~10.6 weeks (~2.5 months) of full-team delivery, which is a reasonable timeline for a 202-point backlog with 4 people, and keeps each role's hours proportional to its FTE (Backend gets the largest share, QA and DevOps deliberately thin given their low FTE, consistent with the note that QA/DevOps are constrained resources).

Non-labour costs include Stripe integration sandbox/production fees setup, staging cloud infra, and a data-migration one-off tooling/license cost for the Oracle extraction, plus a contingency-free CI/CD tooling subscription for the project duration.

Priority breakdown allocates cost roughly proportional to points-weighted-by-priority across Urgent/High/Medium/Low buckets using the same blended rate structure.

Scenarios: P50 (most likely, base estimate), P80 (with typical schedule/scope slippage buffer of ~20%), P95 (worst case accounting for migration and payment integration complexity risk, +40%).

Assumption: no historical actuals available yet for this project, so estimate is grounded in story-point-to-hour heuristics and standard team-ratios, not empirical velocity data.

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration setup, sandbox/production account fees and PCI compliance review
Staging/CI cloud infrastructure (compute, storage) for project duration
Legacy Oracle data extraction tooling and one-off migration licenses
Observability/tracing tooling subscription (e.g. APM) for project duration
Third-party accessibility audit (WCAG 2.2 AA certification support)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project yet; estimate is based on story-point-to-hour heuristics (~6 hours/point blended, adjusted up for complex items like migration and payments) rather than empirical velocity.

1 story point ≈ 6 hours of blended engineering effort as a starting heuristic, with additional hours added for PW-7 (payments) and PW-8 (migration) due to known integration/data-risk complexity beyond raw point count.

QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) and DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) are thinly staffed relative to the 24-item backlog; their allocated hours are capped proportionate to available capacity (~24 hrs/week and ~16 hrs/week respectively), meaning QA and DevOps work will need to be tightly prioritized or the timeline extended.

Backend Developer (1.5 FTE) carries the largest hour allocation given the backend-heavy nature of auth, RBAC, payments, migration, audit log, email service, search, multi-currency, and rate limiting work.
Frontend Developer (1.0 FTE) hours cover design system, dashboard, invoice UI, ticket UI, admin back-office, analytics UI, responsive layout and accessibility pass.

Team capacity (~140 hrs/week combined across all 4 roles) implies a delivery timeline of roughly 10-11 weeks for the full backlog at the base estimate; this is a capacity-driven schedule assumption, not a contractual deadline.

Non-labour costs are one-off/project-duration estimates for third-party tooling and services (Stripe, cloud infra, migration tooling, observability, accessibility audit) and do not include ongoing post-launch operational costs.
Priority breakdown costs are allocated proportionally based on story points within each priority tier, weighted toward the same blended rate structure used for labour lines.
P80 and P95 scenarios add contingency buffers of ~20% and ~40% respectively over the P50 base, reflecting typical schedule slippage and the specific integration/data-migration risks in PW-7 and PW-8.
Rates and roles are taken exactly as given in the rate card; no market-rate substitution was applied.

reductions.description: Descope PW-18 (Admin back-office for support staff, Low priority, 13 points) to a later phase; support agents can use direct DB/read-only tools in the interim.
reductions.effect: Removes ~85 Frontend + 40 Backend hours from this phase

reductions.description: Descope PW-19 (Usage analytics and reporting, Low priority, 8 points) and PW-23 (Contract tests against helpdesk API, Low priority, 5 points); both are non-critical for launch.
reductions.effect: Removes low-priority backend/frontend/QA hours tied to reporting and contract testing

reductions.description: Defer PW-14 (Multi-currency support, Medium, 13 points) to post-launch; launch with single-currency (USD) support only for initial customer base.
reductions.effect: Removes backend FX-rate integration and frontend currency-display work from this phase

reductions.description: Reduce QA Engineer allocation on low-risk, low-priority items (PW-12, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24) by relying on developer self-testing and lighter smoke tests instead of full QA cycles.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~50 QA hours from low-priority backlog items

reductions.description: Defer PW-24 (Decommission legacy portal, Low priority, 8 points) until after the new portal has been live and stable for a defined bake-in period, avoiding parallel DevOps effort during the crunch phase.
reductions.effect: Removes ~40 DevOps hours from this phase, shifting decommission cost to a later, separate budget cycle
